new_items.title: Sub-second dopamine reinforcement shapes juvenile social play.
new_items.summary_rss: Juvenile social play is critical for neurodevelopment, yet the neural mechanisms organizing moment-to-moment interactions remain elusive. Using social behavior sequencing (Social-seq)-an occlusion-robust 3D pose estimation and unsupervised clustering pipeline-we found that nucleus accumbens (NAc) dopamine was tightly coupled to sub-second social syllables during naturalistic interactions. In wild-type juveniles, males exhibited a sharper dopaminergic contrast between proactive play and forced submission than females did, consistent with sex-divergent play strategies. In Shank3-deficient autism models, this process was fundamentally corrupted: proactive play-evoked dopamine responses were abolished in males and significantly sign-inverted in females, with male-specific enhancements during non-social behaviors, driving social play deficits. A multi-agent reinforcement learning model parameterized by disrupted, play-related dopaminergic reinforcement values recapitulated mutant phenotypes. Closed-loop optogenetic stimulation of ventral tegmental area (VTA)-NAc dopamine projections, time-locked to proactive play, restored reciprocal play in Shank3-deficient rats. Sub-second dopaminergic reinforcement thus orchestrates naturalistic social behavior, providing a behaviorally contingent interventional framework for neurodevelopmental disorders.

A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment.
new_items.summary_rss: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

new_items.title: Early epidemiological and spatial assessment of the Bundibugyo virus outbreak 2026.
new_items.summary_rss: A Bundibugyo virus outbreak was first reported on May 15th, 2026 in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with multiple cases reported across health zones during the early phase of the outbreak and suggestions of circulation weeks prior to detection. We pair highly resolved case and testing records with human mobility data to investigate the early outbreak dynamics of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD). We show that human movement was a principle driver of early spatial expansion between May 10th and June 1st when the number of health zones and health areas reporting positive cases increased by 12 and 49, respectively. The early doubling time was estimated at ~10 days. Our work shows the rapid spatial expansion and growth of BVD with implications for intervention strategies.

new_items.title: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome outbreak linked to cruise ship travel in April-May 2026.
new_items.summary_rss: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. The outbreak represents the international displacement of a virus already known to be capable, under specific conditions, to transmit among humans, and does not suggest emergence of a unusual viral strain.

new_items.title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak.
new_items.summary_rss: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

new_items.title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space.
new_items.summary_rss: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.
